candidates.computation_change_reason: The table presents multiple parallel limit types (ambient aquatic acute/chronic, human health, concentration, and mass load) with different units. Interpreting which column(s) represent enforceable permit discharge limits versus reference criteria, and whether comparison is by concentration or load, would change which numeric limit applies and whether monitoring results are compared at all.

Numeric values appear in Chronic Aquatic, Daily Max Conc, Monthly Avg Conc, Daily Max Total, Mon. Avg Total, and load columns. Different readings of which column is operative—or whether these are enforceable limits at all—would change the applicable limit and any exceedance determination for aluminum measurements.

Multiple distinct numeric limits are listed (acute aquatic, daily max, monthly average, and load). Choosing acute versus chronic/average versus load-based limits, or treating the row as non-operative reference values, would yield different compliance outcomes for cadmium.

Acute aquatic (22), daily max (22), and monthly average (14.66666667) limits differ. Interpreting whether compliance is judged on daily maximum or monthly average—and whether the acute aquatic value governs—would change exceedance results for cyanide.

Human-health-based concentration and load limits are present with scientific-notation values and both daily-max and monthly-average forms. Interpretation of which metric applies, and rounding/precision handling, could change whether a reported dioxin measurement exceeds the applicable limit.

The "(P)" designation appears on several metals rows. If interpreted as a priority-pollutant or permit-specific monitoring trigger rather than a numeric limit indicator, it could change whether numeric compliance comparison is applicable (Purpose A) and whether monitoring was required even where all limit cells are N/A (Purpose B).
